title: Integral localization has invertible counit on rational modules
statement: Let ℓ be prime, E a normed extension of Q_ℓ, and X a scheme. For the integral-to-rational coefficient morphism of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], the extension/restriction adjunction counit Ext(Res(P))→P is invertible for every rational module P on X.

source.place: Section 6.8, coefficient localization and Lemma 6.8.13, first paragraph; agent intersection/matrix variant

proof.text: For any scalar telescope whose source and colimit vertex have invertible ℓ, construct the inverse to its zeroth leg using the cocone of inverse powers of ℓ. Colimit extensionality and determination by the zeroth leg prove the inverse identities.

Apply this to the localization-unit telescope of Res(P). Its zeroth leg is the adjunction unit and ℓ is invertible on the restricted rational source and target. The right triangle identity makes the restricted counit invertible. Faithfulness of restriction reflects mono and epi, hence invertibility in the abelian module category.

lean.statement:
theorem integralScalarCounit_isIso (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (E : Type) [NormedField E] [NormedAlgebra ℚ_[ℓ] E]
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (P : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E) X)) :
    IsIso ((Mod.extendRestrictAdjunction
      (coefficientMap (integralScalarMap ℓ E) X)).counit.app P)
